basis: The functional change is byte-identical in both: `cp WN` -> `cp WP` at the same site in movegen.inc. Nothing in either diff shows a specification file, proof obligation, conformance/regression test, property name, or counterexample, so there is no artifact-level evidence of a formal process. The only discriminator is annotation style. Y adds a block comment above the mkHalf body that states the rule as a complete invariant over three exhaustive cases ("reset on a PAWN move (WP) or a capture, else +1") and then discharges the one case-coverage obligation the encoding raises ("`and 7` strips the colour bit, so WP covers black pawns too") - stating the property, then justifying that the representation covers every case, is the residue a spec-and-proof workflow tends to leave. X instead attaches per-instruction trailing labels ("; a PAWN move resets the fifty-move clock", "; so does a capture", the latter on an otherwise-unchanged line), which describe what each line does without ever stating the whole rule or addressing colour coverage; X is also marginally less minimal for touching that unchanged line purely to comment it. This is comment-prose stylistics only - a careful ordinary developer writing a good review comment plausibly produces Y's text - so the signal is weak and I would not defend it strongly; "cannot tell" is close to equally defensible here.
